hook: Did you know that in the EU, over 1,300 food additives are approved — but only about 40 are considered truly safe by independent research groups?
Titanium dioxide (E171) — used to whiten toothpaste, sunscreen, and candy — was banned in EU foods in 2022 due to genotoxicity concerns.
More than 80% of packaged foods in the US contain added sugar — often hidden under 60+ different names.
The average lipstick contains over 20 chemicals. Some studies show women ingest about 4 pounds of lipstick in their lifetime.
Palm oil is in about 50% of packaged supermarket products — and its production is a leading cause of deforestation.
Parabens, commonly used as preservatives in cosmetics, have been found in 99% of breast cancer tissue samples tested in one study.
Artificial food dyes (Red 40, Yellow 5, Blue 1) are derived from petroleum and have been linked to hyperactivity in children.
Microwave popcorn bags are often lined with PFAS (forever chemicals) that leach into the popcorn when heated.
The term 'fragrance' on a label can hide hundreds of undisclosed chemicals — manufacturers aren't required to list them.
Sunscreen ingredients like oxybenzone are absorbed into the bloodstream at levels 400x higher than the FDA's threshold of concern.
Carrageenan, found in many dairy alternatives, is a known gut irritant linked to inflammation and digestive issues.
The 'natural flavor' on your food label could contain up to 100 different chemical compounds — and doesn't have to be natural.
In Europe, over 1,600 chemicals are banned from cosmetics. In the US? Only 11.
Bisphenol A (BPA) — found in can linings, receipts, and plastic bottles — is an endocrine disruptor linked to infertility.
The darker your toast, the more acrylamide — a potential carcinogen formed when starchy foods are cooked at high temperatures.
Your shampoo's sulfates (SLS/SLES) strip natural oils and can cause long-term scalp irritation — yet they're in 90% of shampoos.
1 in 3 sunscreens tested by Consumer Reports didn't actually meet their claimed SPF level.
The 'health halo' around organic junk food is real — organic sugar is still sugar, and organic cookies are still cookies.
Formaldehyde-releasing preservatives are still used in some 'natural' beauty products despite being classified as a human carcinogen.
The Nutri-Score system, used across Europe, rates products on a scale from A (best) to E (worst) — but even an 'A' can contain additives.
Canned foods often contain BPA in the lining. Look for 'BPA-free' cans — or better yet, choose glass jars or fresh.
The average European has 128 different chemicals from personal care products in their body at any given time.
Propylene glycol, used in antifreeze, is also found in many moisturizers and processed foods as a humectant.
High-fructose corn syrup was almost non-existent in 1970. Today, the average American consumes about 25 pounds of it per year.
Microplastics have been found in human blood, lungs, and even placentas — much of it from packaged food containers.
The term 'hypoallergenic' on beauty products is completely unregulated — it means absolutely nothing legally.
